newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Argonaut says tanker market looks good.
newsitem.headline: Argonaut says tanker market looks good.

text.p: Swedish tanker group Argonaut on Monday posted a pre-tax profit of 68 million crowns for the first half of 1997 compared to a loss of 38 million crowns a year ago and said it expected the tanker market to improve further.
The result included a 56 million crown profit from the sale of an Ultra Large Crude Carrier (ULCC).
"Against a background of continuing market strengthening during the summer, we are expecting a further improvement in the shipping result in the third quarter," Argonaut said in a statement.
Turnover in the six months ending June 30 rose to 408 million crowns from 335 million.
Argonaut's average rates for ULCC and VLCC ships rose to $27,900 a day against $24,000.
In the first half two ships were out of the water for 75 days for docking and upgrading, which cut the daily rate average by about $1,100.
Argonaut's VLCC ships had an average rate of $29,700 in the first half, an improvement from $27,300 in the same period last year.
The ULCC Kraka is going through a 20-year classification which had a negative effect on six-month earnings by about 30 million crowns.
The tanker market continued to strengthen in the first half with increased demand following a rise in both oil consumption and stocks.
"The conditions are good for a continued improvement in the market over the next years," Argonaut said.
